idea-plugin.name: Jux Language
idea-plugin.description:
Jux Language

License & disclaimer (please read before installing). This plugin and the Jux toolchain are provided FREE OF CHARGE and "AS IS", without warranty of any kind. You use them entirely at your own risk; to the maximum extent permitted by law the authors and XTREME SOFTWARE SOLUTIONS accept no liability for any damages or data loss arising from their use. Jux is pre-release software and may change or contain defects. On first launch the plugin asks you to accept these terms. See juxlang.dev and github.com/xdsswar/juxlang.

Full IDE support for Jux, a Java/C#-shaped language that lowers to Rust. Write familiar class/interface/enum/record syntax and ship native binaries through the Rust toolchain, with a first-class editing experience modelled on IntelliJ's own Java plugin.

Editing & Navigation

  • Native, PSI-based parser (not just TextMate): a real syntax tree powers the Structure View, breadcrumbs, code folding, and brace matching
  • Customizable syntax highlighting for keywords, types, strings, comments and annotations, with a dedicated color-settings page
  • Go to Declaration, Find Usages, and Rename for in-file declarations; cross-file and Rust-std symbols resolve through the language server
  • Java-like editor behaviour: Complete Current Statement (Ctrl+Shift+Enter) closes brackets, adds the missing ; or opens a { } body; Auto-Indent (Ctrl+Alt+I), auto-closing quotes/brackets, and line/block comment toggling
  • Parameter Info (Ctrl+P) for calls and constructors, listing every overload with the active parameter in bold
  • Surround With (Ctrl+Alt+T): if, while, for, try/catch, unsafe { } and more, plus (expr) / !(expr) over a selected expression
  • Move Statement Up/Down (Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down): moves whole statements and whole members, and will not lift one out of its block
  • Type Hierarchy (Ctrl+H) with supertype, subtype and combined views
  • Spellchecking of comments, plain strings and declaration names (interpolation holes stay code, not prose)
  • Optimize Imports (Ctrl+Alt+O): removes unused and duplicate imports and sorts the rest, just like Java

Refactoring

  • Extract Variable (Ctrl+Alt+V): hoists the selected expression into a var, replaces every occurrence, and opens an in-place rename
  • Introduce Constant (Ctrl+Alt+C): a private static final field on the enclosing type, with the type read off the source
  • Inline Variable (Ctrl+Alt+N): with guards against reassignment and side effects, and parentheses where precedence needs them
  • Safe Delete for any declaration, listing the usages that would break before anything is removed
  • Rename, in place for locals and parameters

Code Generation (Alt+Insert)

  • Generate a constructor, getters, and setters from a class's fields
  • Override / Implement Methods: stubs for inherited methods not yet declared, walking the supertype chain

Intelligence (via juxc-lsp)

  • Live diagnostics with precise Jux error codes: workspace-aware, so cross-file and cross-package errors surface on the right file
  • Completion over keywords, project types, and receiver-aware members, with auto-import on accept and import quick-fixes
  • Hover showing inferred expression types and declaration signatures
  • Autocomplete and auto-import over the Rust standard library and any bound Rust crate, rendered in Jux syntax, indexed automatically from your toolchain and project dependencies

Project & Build

  • New → Jux Project, New → Jux File (Class / Interface / Enum / Struct / Record / Annotation) and New → Jux Package, with package inferred from the source-root-relative path
  • Jux tool window (right side, like Gradle/Cargo): one-click Build, Run, Test, Build Release and Check over a live console
  • Run configurations that auto-detect any file with a main and wire up the gutter Run action
  • IDE-wide toolchain settings (Settings | Tools | Jux Toolchain): auto-detects juxc / jux / juxc-lsp from $JUX_HOME, PATH, and common install locations

Works in every IntelliJ-platform IDE (IDEA, CLion, RustRover, GoLand, PyCharm, …). Language-server features use the IDE's built-in LSP client where available (commercial IDEs and IDEA free mode 2025.2+); on Community editions, install the free LSP4IJ plugin and the same features light up through it. When both clients are available the built-in one takes precedence automatically, so only one juxc-lsp instance ever runs.
